questions.question: In which year was the Treaty of Amritsar signed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1809.
  • The Treaty of Amritsar was signed in 1809 between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and the British (Charles Metcalfe).
  • It fixed the Sutlej River as the boundary between the Sikh Empire and British India.
  • This treaty prevented Ranjit Singh from expanding eastward.

questions.question: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1931.
  • The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on March 5, 1931, before the Second Round Table Conference.
  • Gandhiji agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement.
  • The British agreed to release non-violent political prisoners and allow salt manufacture for personal use.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding Gautama Buddha?

I. Siddhartha, also known as Gautama, the founder of Buddhism, was born about 2500 years ago.

II. The Gautama Buddha belonged to a small gana known as the Sakya gana.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both I and II.
  • Siddhartha (Gautama) was indeed born about 2500 years ago (c. 563 BCE).
  • He belonged to the Sakya Gana and was a Kshatriya prince.
  • He left home at 29 in search of truth, known as Mahabhinishkramana.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre, took place in consequence to the protest against the __________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rowlatt Act.
  • (Context repetition) The protest in Jallianwala Bagh was specifically against the repressive Rowlatt Act.
  • The act allowed the British to imprison anyone without trial.
  • This event was the turning point that led to the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.question: Which of the following Mauryan inscriptions is NOT located in present-day India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kandahar.
  • The Kandahar Inscription (Bilingual: Greek and Aramaic) is located in Afghanistan.
  • Kalsi (Uttarakhand), Girnar (Gujarat), and Maski (Karnataka) are in present-day India.
  • Ashoka's edicts have been found across India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Nepal.

questions.question: Into how many distinctive types of territories was the Harshvardhan’s Dynasty divided?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Two.
  • Harshavardhana’s administration divided territories into directly governed provinces and tributary states (under Samantas).
  • The directly administered regions were called Bhuktis.
  • He held a massive assembly at Prayag every five years.

questions.question: The capital of the Mauryan empire was ___________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pataliputra.
  • Pataliputra was the main capital of the Mauryan Empire.
  • Other important provincial capitals included Taxila (NW), Ujjain (Central), Tosali (East), and Suvarnagiri (South).
  • The city was famous for its massive wooden fortifications.

questions.question: Which of the following war/battle is associated with the hanging of Mangal Pandey?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Indian Rebellion of 1857.
  • Mangal Pandey was a sepoy in the 34th Bengal Native Infantry.
  • He revolted at Barrackpore on March 29, 1857, by attacking British officers.
  • His execution on April 8, 1857, acted as a catalyst for the Great Revolt.

questions.question: In 1919, Gandhiji called for a satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act that curbed ____________ such as the freedom of expression.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is fundamental rights.
  • Gandhiji argued that the Rowlatt Act attacked fundamental rights like freedom of expression.
  • It gave the police power to search without warrant and detain without trial.
  • He organized the Rowlatt Satyagraha, the first all-India struggle against British rule.

questions.question: During ancient India in the Tamil region, ordinary ploughmen were known as ____________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is uzhavar.
  • In ancient Tamil society (Sangam Age):
    • Vellalar: Large landowners.
    • Uzhavar: Ordinary ploughmen.
    • Kadaisiyar/Adimai: Landless laborers and slaves.

questions.question: The Vice-President of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of which legislative body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rajya Sabha.
  • The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
  • This is defined under Article 64 of the Indian Constitution.
  • He presides over the proceedings of the upper house.

questions.question: Megasthenes wrote about Pataliputra, saying that it is a large and beautiful city that is surrounded by a massive wall. It has 570 towers and __________ gates.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 64.
  • As per Megasthenes' Indica, the city of Pataliputra had 64 gates and 570 towers.
  • The city was shaped like a parallelogram and protected by a deep moat.
  • The royal palace was built of wood but highly decorated.

questions.question: Who among the following was associated with the Young Bengal Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Henry Derozio.
  • Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, a teacher at Hindu College, founded the Young Bengal Movement.
  • His followers (Derozians) were inspired by the French Revolution and radical thinking.
  • They advocated for women's rights and freedom of expression.

questions.question: The Simon Commission arrived in India in __________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1928.
  • The Simon Commission (Statutory Commission) arrived in India in 1928.
  • It was met with chants of 'Simon Go Back' because it had no Indian members.
  • Lala Lajpat Rai died from injuries during a lathi charge protesting this commission in Lahore.

questions.question: On the bank of now dry course of which river, the ancient city of Harappa was built?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ravi.
  • The ancient city of Harappa was located on the banks of the Ravi River (in present-day Pakistan).
  • It was the first site of the Indus Valley Civilization to be excavated (1921).
  • Daya Ram Sahni led the excavation.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Mauryan empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chandragupta Maurya.
  • (Repetition) Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire in 322 BC after defeating Dhana Nanda.
  • His empire stretched from Afghanistan to the Deccan.
  • He spent his final days as a Jaina ascetic in Shravanabelagola.

questions.question: Tipu Sultan became the ruler of Mysore in _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1782.
  • Tipu Sultan (The Tiger of Mysore) became the ruler after the death of his father, Hyder Ali, in 1782.
  • He fought four Anglo-Mysore Wars.
  • He died in 1799 defending his capital, Seringapatam.

questions.question: Who is known as the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" and played a pivotal role in the Bengal Renaissance movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
  • He is known as the 'Father of Indian Renaissance' for his role in modernizing Indian society.
  • He worked for the abolition of Sati and advocated for English education.
  • He founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828.

questions.question: The city of _________ was located on Khadir Beyt (also spelled as Bet) in the Rann of Kutch, where there was fresh water and fertile soil.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dholavira.
  • Dholavira is located on Khadir Bet in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.
  • Unlike other Harappan cities (divided into 2 parts), Dholavira was divided into three parts.
  • It is famous for its gigantic water reservoirs and an ancient 'signboard'.

questions.question: In which year was the Dandi March by Mahatma Gandhi launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1930.
  • (Repetition) The Dandi March was launched on March 12, 1930.
  • It lasted 24 days and covered about 240 miles.
  • It challenged the Salt Law and sparked nationwide protests.

questions.question: A famous play, ‘Abhijnana Shakuntalam’ was written by which of the following personalities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kalidasa.
  • Abhijnana Shakuntalam (The Recognition of Shakuntala) is the most famous Sanskrit drama by Kalidasa.
  • Kalidasa was one of the 'Nine Gems' (Navaratnas) in the court of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).
  • His works represent the peak of Classical Sanskrit literature.

questions.question: In which year did Cripps Mission arrive in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1942.
  • The Cripps Mission, led by Sir Stafford Cripps, came to India in March 1942.
  • It aimed to secure Indian support for World War II.
  • The mission failed, leading Gandhiji to launch the Quit India Movement.

questions.question: The oldest Veda is the Rigveda, composed about ________ years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 3500.
  • The Rigveda is the oldest Veda, composed around 1500 BCE (about 3500 years ago).
  • It contains 1028 hymns (Suktas) and is divided into 10 Mandalas.
  • It is a primary source for the Early Vedic Period.

questions.question: In which year was the Second Anglo-Burmese War fought?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1852.
  • The Second Anglo-Burmese War took place in 1852 under Lord Dalhousie.
  • It resulted in the British annexation of Lower Burma (Pegu).
  • The conflict arose due to disputes between British merchants and the Burmese governor.

questions.question: Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Brihadratha.
  • Brihadratha was the last ruler of the Mauryan Empire.
  • He was assassinated in 185 BC by his commander-in-chief, Pushyamitra Shunga.
  • This marked the end of the Maurya dynasty and the rise of the Shunga dynasty.
